mechanism: Scopolamine's anticholinergic effects may impair gastric motility and reduce sirolimus absorption, while both drugs can cause CNS effects; sirolimus is a CYP3A4 substrate and scopolamine is metabolized hepatically with potential for additive CNS depression.
action: Monitor sirolimus therapeutic levels closely; consider alternative antimuscarinic agents if possible; counsel patient on additive CNS depression risks (dizziness, drowsiness) and avoid activities requiring alertness.
